FailList.Trigger: A grading capture is accepted, and the operator (who holds the unblinding map) can see an unfavorable result. The operator then submits a distinct re-export, opens a second session in the review workspace, or sends a malformed LockBlindGrades request.
FailList.Problem: Each of those actions records GradingInvalid. §21.1 makes no exception for an attempt whose capture is already accepted, and any LockBlindGrades 400 counts the same way. Attempt1 is then allowed after GradingInvalid and before any lock. §23 explicitly accepts 'server-recorded GradingInvalid' as an exit for an accepted capture. So a valid, unlocked grading can be turned into an invalid one by a legitimate-looking call, and the same runs regraded. Only the post-lock case (L2276-2278) is protected.
FailList.Consequence: The operator gets one extra blind-grading draw over the same runs, chosen after the result is known, for the evaluation that gates activation. The accounting discloses it but nothing prevents it. This contradicts 'No regrade follows a valid low score'. My R12-01 wording ('or GradingInvalid') left this path open.
FailList.RequiredResolution: In §21.1 and §23, apply the existing post-lock rule from the moment a capture is accepted: a later session or distinct capture for that attempt is recorded in accounting, does not convert the attempt to GradingInvalid, grants no Attempt1, and refuses activation for that workspace/policy/build. State that aborting a grader before it terminates successfully looks the same as a crash and remains an operator-attested residual, disclosed through session and attempt accounting. Reword L2242 to say that no regrade follows an accepted capture except after a LockBlindGrades content failure.
